features.text: Encoder counts: how two interrupt pins turn wheel rotation into a speed you can read.
A PI loop: the step response shows rise time, overshoot and settling time.
Loop timing: a slow loop makes the same gains oscillate.

hints: The speed reads the wrong way round: one encoder runs backward. Check the left encoder channels A and B.
The speed keeps swinging around the target: look at the loop period on pin 13. A slow loop turns the same gains into an oscillation.
The robot resets as soon as the motors start: look at the battery voltage while the motors start.
The robot veers or turns the wrong way: one motor runs backward. Check the left motor leads.
The left wheel spins and the speed reads low: the wheel is slipping, so look at the grip under it.
Still stuck? Compare each reading with the run before you changed anything.
guide.lede: A two-wheel robot that holds 0.2 m/s with encoders and a PI loop, and a step response you can tune.
guide.overview: Each gear motor now has an encoder. The Uno counts the pulses on interrupt pins, turns the counts into a speed and adjusts the PWM so the speed settles on the target. Change the gains and watch the step response.

specs.label: Motors
specs.value: Two TT gear motors with encoders, 48:1

specs.label: Encoder
specs.value: 11 pulses per motor revolution, 528 per wheel revolution (iynk assumption)

specs.label: What it models
specs.value: Motor torque and back-EMF, the gearbox, encoder edges, wheel grip, battery sag and loop timing. It does not model encoder noise or wheel flex.

steps: Build the drive base, then use the motors with encoders. Wire each encoder's V to 5 V and G to ground.
Wire the left encoder A to D2 and B to D11, and the right encoder A to D3 and B to D12.
Press Run. The target steps from 0 to 0.2 m/s at 2 s and the PID panel draws the step response.
Change KP and KI in the sketch and run again: watch rise time, overshoot and settling time move.
Open the loop timing view, then enable the slow loop fault and run again.
guide.title: Speed control

meta.description: The drive base with a two-channel encoder on each gear motor. The sketch counts encoder edges with interrupts, works out the speed and holds 0.2 m/s with a PI loop; the target steps from 0 at 2 s. Part values are iynk assumptions unless a part says otherwise.
meta.title: Speed control

faults.note: Weak pack: the Uno resets when both motors start.
The left encoder channels are swapped: the left count runs backward, so the speed estimate is wrong.
Swaps the left motor leads: the left wheel turns the wrong way, so the robot veers and the turn comes out wrong.
A delay(40) in loop(): the loop runs at half the rate the gains were tuned for, and the speed oscillates.
The left wheel grips a quarter as well: it spins and the robot drifts.
